I was sitting here going, one of the biggest lies that makes me so angry that people keep repeating, and there is no truth to this, there's no truth to this, is that Tyler Robinson's dad handed him in, that Tyler Robinson confessed to the crime, and there's not a shred of proof to this. First and foremost, it does not pass the common sense test, okay?

verification.notes: Utah's criminal information directly contradicts the no-evidence claim: it says Robinson's parents believed he matched the suspect, his father asked about the rifle, Robinson implied he was the shooter, and the parents and a retired-deputy family friend convinced him to surrender. The filing also quotes alleged admissions to his roommate. These remain prosecution allegations, but they are plainly evidence.

records.text: At least five other sets of prints were found on the rifle, Tyler Robinson's prints were the most degraded, and prints from the owner and Lance Twiggs were also present
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We were told Tyler Robinson's gun had had DNA all over it. And I'm going to call that a lie by severe omission because every time they said this in the public, they refused to say but five other sets of prints minimally were also found on the gun and they refused to say that Tyler's are the most degraded. Tyler's prints are the most degradative. All the prints that were found on this gun, that is a severe lie by omission to continually say they found his prints on a gun and not admit that five other sets were found of which one were his owned by his father and the other by Lance (Lance Twiggs).

verification.notes: The statement conflates DNA mixtures with fingerprints and misstates the contributors. The hearing evidence discussed DNA swabs, not five other sets of prints on the rifle. It described a trigger/guard mixture consistent with at least four contributors including Robinson; Matthew Robinson had support for inclusion on rifle-bolt swabs; and Twiggs had support for inclusion on the Dremel tool, not the rifle. The major Robinson profile showed degradation, but the compound print claim is directly contradicted.

records.text: Candace Owens reported that Matt Robinson suspected federal agents had staged Tyler Robinson's room by placing a dog bed there.

verification.notes: Corrects an attribution-only true rating. Owens paraphrases a suspicion attributed to Matt Robinson. No directly attributable interview, original room inventory, before/after scene record, or custody evidence was located corroborating his reported suspicion or federal staging. A supposed persona does not establish dog-bed ownership.
